Trail Physics · Unit 5: Bike Mechanics · Module 13

Rotational Dynamics

Angular velocity and acceleration, torque, moment of inertia, gear ratios and rotational energy.

Lesson coming

The question

Why does the easiest gear make climbing feel lighter, but slower?

The physics

  • Angular displacement, velocity and acceleration
  • Torque
  • Moment of inertia
  • Rotational equilibrium
  • Rotational kinetic energy
  • Mechanical advantage

The math

  • τ = rF sin θ
  • ω = v / r
  • gear ratio = chainring teeth ÷ cog teeth
  • KE_rot = ½Iω²

Learning objectives

  • Relate angular velocity, linear speed and radius
  • Calculate a gear ratio and explain mechanical advantage
  • Follow rotation from crank to wheel to find distance and speed
  • Calculate torque from a force and a lever arm
  • Explain moment of inertia and why wheel mass matters
  • Calculate rotational kinetic energy

Helps to know first: Uniform Circular Motion, Work and Power.

The mountain biking connection

Cranks, chainrings, cassettes, wheels and brake rotors all rotate. Torque at the pedals becomes torque at the wheel, multiplied or divided by the gear ratio.
